title: Parker playing along with the radio, and the idea of genius
summary: Parker in his hotel room plays with any radio music; Malachi puts him with Toby Walker, Tatum and later Erroll Garner as geniuses.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: It was nothing to walk into Charlie's hotel room early in the morning and find him walking around with nothing on except maybe a towel tied around his waist, and his radio playing, and it could be a symphony orchestra, it could be anything on the radio playing, and he'd be playing his horn right along with it. It got so that everybody would go around to his room, sit down and just listen to him play!

He was just one of those other people that I just felt like was a genius. I mentioned years ago about this fellow Toby Walker. Well, Charlie Parker was another one of those people that just had something different about him. I just never met anyone like that. Of course, I've always felt like Art Tatum had that same kind of a thing. There were just things that were beyond understanding of what or how he did them, or how they came about, or how they came to be. Because it certainly wasn't a lot of things that you could just sit down and figure out.
Later, after hearing Erroll Garner, I really began to feel that way about him. And I want to talk about Erroll Garner a little later.
